title.narrative: Digital Transformation of Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) Reporting and Pharmacovigilance System in Viet Nam

description.narrative:
This project will deliver core modules of a secure digital platform for ADR reporting and pharmacovigilance in Viet Nam, to the point of initial testing and piloting. Through four integrated Activities, the project will map current regulatory processes, provide pharmacovigilance advisory support, develop and deploy core modules of a modern ADR system, and build local capacity to use it.
First, the ADR Centre’s workflows and requirements will be analysed in detail, producing process maps and technical specifications for optimal system design. Next, priority regulatory processes and data flows interfacing with pharmacovigilance will be documented, ensuring the new system fits into broader medicines regulation. Based on these designs, an E2B(R3)-standards-compliant ADR digital system will be developed. Existing ADR data will be standardised and migrated. Necessary hardware will be procured. The system will be tested and piloted, and initial training provided to pharmacovigilance staff. Pharmacovigilance technical advice will be provided, including in relation to use of high-quality ADR data in HTA.
These Outputs will directly achieve the project Purpose by improving data timeliness and quality, creating real-world impact as regulators can more quickly identify safety problems, more efficiently engage industry, and protect patients. Importantly, the detailed process mapping will guide future investments in digitalising Viet Nam’s medicine regulatory system, making this a catalytic project for larger-scale innovation.
